description.value: An event-related fMRI study investigated how emotional arousal modulates neural responses to negative and neutral pictures in healthy young and older adults.

spans.text: The present event-related fMRI study used a broader range of negative emotional stimuli (low, medium, and high arousing) to test the hypothesis that emotional functioning in aging is modulated by the level of arousal, and to identify the associated neural correlates.

we predicted that opposing patterns of response in the ACC/vmPFC (increased) vs. amygdala (decreased) would be specific to low arousing stimuli.
we explored the possibility that increased activity in this region would be linked to reduced ratings for low arousing negative stimuli in older adults.

description.value: Participants viewed and rated negative and neutral pictures during fMRI recording.

spans.text: Functional MR images were recorded while participants viewed and rated negative and neutral images.

The present event-related fMRI study used a broader range of negative emotional stimuli (low, medium, and high arousing) to test the hypothesis that emotional functioning in aging is modulated by the level of arousal, and to identify the associated neural correlates.
Responses were recorded using a 4-button response box

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to watch the pictures, experience any feelings or thoughts they triggered, and rate their subjective emotional experience after becoming aware of the picture content and their emotional response. They were encouraged to rate while the picture was displayed, or during the fixation screen if more time was needed. In the first run, they were not given an explicit goal to regulate emotions.

spans.text: Participants were instructed to rate the pictures only after they were aware of the content of the picture and of their emotional response to the picture.

stimuli.value: 180 pictures: 90 negative and 90 neutral images, including IAPS pictures and additional neutral pictures from other sources. Negative pictures were divided into equal low-, medium-, and high-arousal groups.

spans.text: Stimuli presented during the scanning session consisted of 180 pictures (90 negative and 90 neutral)

spans.text: Participants were asked to watch the pictures and rate their subjective emotional experience triggered by the pictures on an 8-point scale (1 = neutral, 8 = extremely negative).
